source_review.notes: Checked all nine structured references at dbt Labs, PostgreSQL, Google Cloud, OpenLineage, and SQLite; every URL returned HTTP 200. Claims about dbt SQL models, ref-derived DAGs and data tests; PostgreSQL CTE, window and CREATE TABLE AS behavior; BigQuery transaction scope; OpenLineage Job/Run/Dataset identity; and SQLite window syntax match the cited current documentation and remain explicitly product/version scoped.

Checked bag multiplicities a_k and b_k, gate predicate A_v, expected-prior conditional publication, and deterministic equivalence relation for type-consistent use.
Draft chapter validation accepted the exact front matter, H1, H2/H3 contract, local links, and GitHub-compatible inline/display math.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical model, physical relation, run attempt, candidate generation, trusted publication, and consumer-visible identity remain separate throughout.

evidence: Executed the finite SQL against an in-memory SQLite database: outputs are c1=(2 orders, 1700 gross, 300 refund, 1400 net) and c2=(1, 800, 100, 700).

Executed the independently implemented safe Python reference model under two shuffled input orders: 5 typed rows, 1 rejected row, 1 superseded occurrence, 2500 gross, 400 matched refunds, 2100 net, and stable replay.

Recomputed Exercise 2 directly: two order occurrences crossed with three refunds produce 6 rows, gross 3(100+120)=660, refund 2(10+20+5)=70; winner/pre-aggregate output is gross 120, refund 35, net 85.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All explicit row counts, customer measures, fanout totals, and exercise arithmetic reproduce exactly.

evidence: Verified that an acyclic finite graph admits a topological order and every edge u->v then satisfies tau(u)<tau(v); this establishes dependency availability, not semantic correctness or snapshot coherence.
Verified equijoin fanout a_k*b_k and the sufficient at-most-one-result premise a_k<=1 and b_k<=1 after version resolution and many-side pre-aggregation.

Verified the conditional publication transition requires both passing A_v and equality between observed and expected prior pointer, preventing a stale attempt from blindly overwriting a newer generation.
Verified deterministic equivalence is parameterized by engine/session/templates/inputs and does not imply byte-identical physical layout or cross-engine behavior.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The deductions are conditional on declared and enforced/validated graph, key, cut, engine, and publication premises.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review establishes graph and fanout mechanisms; exposition progresses from model/dependency/source contracts through SQL semantics, materialization, tests, publication, operations, tuning, security, and evolution; schematic SQL plus an independent executable reference model make evidence limits visible; and ten examples plus five solved exercises require both calculation and design judgment.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. References and local checks were performed on 2026-09-02. The finite SQLite execution and independent Python reference model do not establish arbitrary-query correctness, production dialect semantics, cross-engine equivalence, source snapshot coherence, dependency completeness, macro/compiler reproducibility, transaction or DDL behavior, atomic publication, idempotent recovery, authorization/privacy compliance, representative plans, performance/cost capacity, lineage completeness, schema-migration safety, or disaster recovery; those require system-specific contracts and deployed evidence.
